verdict: No scientific blocker to the proposed same-family viscoelastic revision. This approves the bounded prototype, not a final task or empirical difficulty.
scope: Read actual corrected prototype source, full report summary and case data, final author ASSESSMENT, preserved tail-error note, and relevant primary-paper sections. Verified all six payload hashes. No numerical or model rerun; no source edits.
derivation: With exp[i(kx-omega t)], the linear viscosity is nu0[beta+(1-beta)/(1-i omega lambda)]. The decaying root s=sqrt(k^2-i omega/viscosity) and anchored transverse-sheet streamfunction satisfy psi(0)=omega/k and psi_prime(0)=0. Velocities u=psi_prime and v=-i k psi have the stated phase.

For G_ij=partial_j u_i, first-order conformation is (G+G^T)/(lambda^(-1)-i omega). Expanding the upper-convected equation gives mean extra polymer stress eta_p times the average of G C+C G^T-u dot grad C. The code correctly forms the harmonic products with one-half real-part factors.
The derivative polymer forcing includes derivatives of both gradient factors and all material-advection factors. Componentwise assembly in the mean BVP has the same tensor orientation and sign.

The mean x-momentum equation is nu0 U_second+Nxy_prime=average(u partial_x u+v partial_y u)=partial_y average(u v), with density one. Zero far-field shear gives nu0 U_prime+Nxy=average(u v). Thus the far-field mean is the wall Taylor value plus integral[average(u v)-Nxy]/nu0.

The source retains the complete first-order Jeffreys response, the correct displaced-wall mean boundary term and the full Reynolds transport term from revision 1. It omits only the nonlinear polymer contribution by extending a laboratory-frame linear viscoelastic law to the second-order mean. This is an explicit physical approximation; it is not an objective corotational fluid model.

Two distinct positive calibration heights provide global identification: (u+i v)(h2)/(u+i v)(h1)=exp[-s(h2-h1)]. The recorded worst phase bound .68851 radians is below pi, removing logarithm aliases. The known complex-viscosity factor then uniquely gives positive nu0. This argument does not assume the real part of s is monotonic in nu0.

reference_scope.independent_parts: Fourth-order harmonic-vorticity BVP and componentwise differentiated forced mean-momentum BVP; no closed harmonic modes or integrated flux oracle in its physical prediction.
reference_scope.shared_parts: Known complex-viscosity law and local velocity/conformation tensor helper are shared. The reference is independent in spatial solution and mean integration, not a fully independent derivation of every constitutive factor.
reference_scope.complementary_checks: Newtonian limits beta=1 or lambda=0, the independent published creeping limit, momentum balance, wall power versus volume dissipation, wave reversal and finite-difference polymer-gradient check support the common algebra.

input_assessment.scope: Actual final author ASSESSMENT read. It specifies geometry, material, units and limit order without a final task interface. No final public task files exist yet; final public input and grader require later review.
input_assessment.necessary_apparatus: Incompressible Oldroyd-B half-space, known solvent fraction and polymer relaxation, fixed material sheet x=X with prescribed transverse traveling displacement, no slip, no imposed pressure gradient or far counterflow/shear, and the stationary small-amplitude Eulerian far-field pumping coefficient. Density and current/reference length/time units must remain explicit.
input_assessment.limit_order: At each finite frequency and relaxation time, take the stable periodic small-amplitude branch; the mean pumping is the coefficient in the stationary far-field response. No high-De limit at fixed nonzero deformation amplitude or unstated swimming/inextensibility constraint is assumed.
input_assessment.readout: Calibration uses signed first-harmonic velocities divided by amplitude. Pumping is lab-frame Eulerian mean divided by amplitude squared; far-field Stokes drift vanishes as harmonic velocities decay. No additional Lagrangian correction belongs in this readout.

primary_source.title: Lauga, Propulsion in a viscoelastic fluid
primary_source.sections_read: Section III.3 equations 19-20; Appendix B equations 64-68 and surrounding text; abstract and linear-response discussion.
primary_source.supports: Nonlinear constitutive terms enter quadratic propulsion; the creeping pumping ratio is (1+beta*De^2)/(1+De^2). Corotational Maxwell is in the family with the same leading pumping. These statements do not directly verify the new finite-inertia numerical solution.

qualifications: The 27-point high-frequency window has healthy positive physical signals and at least 76.3% sampled separation. A broader control has only .1794% gap; it is preserved and no universal full-domain gap is claimed.

The first unweighted-expm1 tail implementation overflowed when Re(s-k)<0; initial nonfinite output and its inadequate aggregate check are preserved as a numerical failure, not physics evidence. Corrected weighted exponentials and explicit finite assertions are used in the current successful source.

The objective corotational alternative is not a discriminator here. For planar incompressible harmonics, the change in stretching contributes an isotropic mean term, absorbable into pressure. Keep the weaker laboratory-linear source limitation explicit in author documentation.
This is a waving-sheet family revision and shares constitutive-objectivity themes with archived dumbbell stress. It is not an unrelated new theoretical principle.
No final calibration dataset, 256-noise study, Docker control, task grading or model evaluation is approved by this prototype review.
